> RESEARCH MODE: research reasoning produced by the cloud model `deepseek-flash`; new implementations and data experiments are permitted; acceptance targets remain fixed.

## LLM research analysis

### Measured facts (this evidence packet)
- Dev release preview (seed 7, pseudo benchmark, subject-group split): train 325 rows / development_test 85; defect support train = blur 72, over_exp 36, under_exp 36, flare 7, white_balance 0; dev_test = blur 18, over_exp 9, under_exp 9, flare 3, white_balance 0; score range 28.0-95.9. final_labels_inspected = false.
- Frozen-protocol reproduction baseline `mobileclip2_v7_score` (KONIQ-trained MobileCLIP2-S0 adapter score head + zero-ROM calibrated measurement defect head) is documented as macro-F1 0.424, PLCC 0.476 on the frozen eval.
- `multitask_adapter.py` DEFAULTS use 60 epochs, above the task max_epochs=40; `config.py` sets MIN_CLASS_SUPPORT=5, floors 0.85/0.90, and resolves pretrained/adapter checkpoints locally (raises FileNotFoundError when absent).
- All eight supplied papers are abstract-only leads (evidence_level=abstract_only_not_reproduced), retrieved 2026-10-15 (publication dates 2018-2026); two were returned empty (recall_lessons: none; search_assets model: none).

### Interpretation (gate feasibility)
With white_balance support 0 in both splits, per-class F1 for that class is undefined (convention scores 0), so 5-class defect_macro_f1 is capped at 4/5 = 0.80 even with four perfect classes: the 0.85 defect gate is structurally unattainable without new labels, and flare (3 dev_test positives < MIN_CLASS_SUPPORT) is statistically unmeasurable. Only PLCC/SRCC/grade_agreement and supported-class defect F1 (blur/over_exp/under_exp) are measurable this run. The exposed historical test set means replication, not independent acceptance.

### Experiments selected (iteration 1)
C1 = reproduce the baseline protocol unchanged (reference point). C2 = new coded method `multitask_adapter_rank`: frozen MobileCLIP2-S0 encoder + shared trunk + score head + 5-logit defect head, trained with Huber + pairwise rank + soft-PLCC loss (leads: ev_65aa194cfa multi-task MOS with PLCC loss; ev_6fb3c850a1 learning-to-rank) and class-balanced focal BCE with prior logit adjustment, val-only isotonic calibration and val-only thresholds, fp16 export (~23.4 MB << 60 MB). Data pilots: 120 hflip-augmented train rows and a 4-sample weak-annotation probe for the missing white_balance class.

### Controls / ablations
A0 baseline; A1 C2 code without augmentation; A2 C2 code with hflip augment (isolates data); A3 score head only (rank/PLCC weights = 0, defect head disabled); A4 fixed 0.5 thresholds and identity calibration vs val-tuned. Same frozen encoder, seed 7 and subject-disjoint val for all; eval labels never touched; headline metrics only from the independent evaluator.

### Falsification and known limits
A val-PLCC gain < 0.02 over A1 falsifies the loss change; a flare/white_balance recall drop under hflip falsifies label-preserving augmentation for those classes; a macro-F1 5-class claim above 0.80 without new labels would indicate a protocol/metric error. Pseudo-MOS is not human MOS (noise level unknown), and ROM here is an fp16 parameter estimate, not a packaged/latency measurement.

### Unknowns
Grade-agreement and hardcase_macro_f1 definitions/slices are not supplied (hardcase unmeasurable as specified); whether grading uses the pseudo benchmark (325/85) or the KonIQ release (610 eval rows) is ambiguous; defect-label provenance is unstated; no registered trusted external source exists for `extend`.

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""MobileCLIP2-S0 + multi-task adapter heads (the main plan-A1 candidate).

Frozen MobileCLIP2-S0 visual encoder (11.41 M params, ~22.8 MB fp16) with two
lightweight trainable heads on the shared 512-d embedding:

* a score head  -> continuous 0-100 quality score (report plan A1);
* a defect head -> 5 independent logits for blur / over_exp / under_exp /
  flare / white_balance (multi-label, class-weighted BCE).

Training uses only the *dev* split (subject-group-disjoint train/val); the
frozen eval split is touched once, for prediction, and the headline metrics are
computed by the independent evaluator, never here.

Everything runs on GPU when available; encoder features are cached so the
self-optimisation loop can re-train heads in seconds.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Tuple

import numpy as np

from . import clip_backbone, common

DEFAULTS: Dict[str, Any] = {
    "epochs": 60,
    "lr": 2e-3,
    "weight_decay": 1e-2,
    "hidden": 256,
    "dropout": 0.15,
    "batch_size": 64,
    "bce_weight": 1.0,
    "l1_weight": 0.5,
    "pos_weight_scale": 1.0,
    "min_pos_weight": 1.0,
    "max_pos_weight": 20.0,
    "defect_threshold": 0.5,
    "tune_thresholds": True,
    "image_size": 256,
    "feature_batch": 32,
}


def _pos_weight(d: np.ndarray, scale: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> np.ndarray:
    pos = d.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
    neg = d.shape[0] - pos
    w = np.where(pos > 0, neg / np.maximum(pos, 1.0), 1.0)
    w = np.clip(w * float(scale), lo, hi)
    return w.astype(np.float32)


def _macro_f1(y: np.ndarray, p: np.ndarray, classes: List[int]) -> float:
    f1s = []
    for c in classes:
        yt, yp = y[:, c], p[:, c]
        tp = int(((yt == 1) & (yp == 1)).sum())
        fp = int(((yt == 0) & (yp == 1)).sum())
        fn = int(((yt == 1) & (yp == 0)).sum())
        prec = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) else 0.0
        rec = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) else 0.0
        f1s.append((2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec)) if (prec + rec) else 0.0)
    return float(np.mean(f1s)) if f1s else 0.0


def _best_thresholds(y: np.ndarray, prob: np.ndarray, classes: List[int]) -> Dict[int, float]:
    thresholds: Dict[int, float] = {}
    grid = np.arange(0.05, 0.96, 0.025)
    for c in classes:
        best_t, best_f1 = 0.5, -1.0
        for t in grid:
            p = (prob[:, c] >= t).astype(int)
            yt = y[:, c]
            tp = int(((yt == 1) & (p == 1)).sum())
            fp = int(((yt == 0) & (p == 1)).sum())
            fn = int(((yt == 1) & (p == 0)).sum())
            prec = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) else 0.0
            rec = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) else 0.0
            f1 = (2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec)) if (prec + rec) else 0.0
            if f1 > best_f1:
                best_f1, best_t = f1, float(t)
        thresholds[c] = best_t
    return thresholds


def _plcc(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:
    if len(a) < 3 or float(np.std(a)) == 0 or float(np.std(b)) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])


def run(ctx, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    import torch
    import torch.nn as nn

    cfg = {**DEFAULTS, **(config or {})}
    C = common.plugin_config()
    dev = common.load_dev(ctx.data_dir)
    inputs = common.load_eval_inputs(ctx.data_dir)
    split = common.load_dev_split(ctx.data_dir)
    device = common.resolve_device() or torch.device("cpu")
    cache = Path(common.cache_dir(ctx))
    t_start = time.time()

    pretrained = C.pretrained_ckpt()
    if not Path(pretrained).exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"MobileCLIP2-S0 pretrained weights missing: {pretrained}")

    dev_paths = [r["path"] for r in dev]
    eval_paths = [r["path"] for r in inputs]

    encoder, preprocess = clip_backbone.build_encoder(pretrained, int(cfg["image_size"]))
    encoder = encoder.to(device)
    X_dev = clip_backbone.extract_features(encoder, preprocess, dev_paths, device,
                                           cache_dir=cache, tag="mobileclip2s0_256",
                                           batch_size=int(cfg["feature_batch"]))
    X_eval = clip_backbone.extract_features(encoder, preprocess, eval_paths, device,
                                            cache_dir=cache, tag="mobileclip2s0_256",
                                            batch_size=int(cfg["feature_batch"]))

    n = len(dev)
    tr_idx = np.asarray(split.get("train") or list(range(n)), dtype=int)
    va_idx = np.asarray(split.get("val") or list(range(n)), dtype=int)
    dim = X_dev.shape[1]

    y_score = np.asarray([float(r.get("score", 0.0)) for r in dev], dtype=np.float32)
    y_def = np.asarray([common.defect_vector(r, C.DEFECTS) for r in dev], dtype=np.float32)
    y_scaled = (y_score - 50.0) / 25.0
    classes = [i for i, d in enumerate(C.DEFECTS) if int(y_def[:, i].sum()) > 0]

    mu, sd = X_dev[tr_idx].mean(axis=0, keepdims=True), X_dev[tr_idx].std(axis=0, keepdims=True) + 1e-6
    Xt = torch.tensor((X_dev - mu) / sd, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    Xe = torch.tensor((X_eval - mu) / sd, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    Yt = torch.tensor(y_scaled, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    Dt = torch.tensor(y_def, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    tr = torch.tensor(tr_idx, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    va = torch.tensor(va_idx, dtype=torch.long, device=device)

    class MultiTaskHead(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, in_dim: int, hidden: int, dropout: float, n_def: int):
            super().__init__()
            self.trunk = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(in_dim, hidden), nn.LayerNorm(hidden), nn.GELU(), nn.Dropout(dropout))
            self.score = nn.Linear(hidden, 1)
            self.defect = nn.Linear(hidden, n_def)

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Real trained score head (iqa_adapter_v7) + measurement defect head.

This is the *reproduction baseline* the iqa_agent engine reported (macro-F1
0.424, PLCC 0.476 on the frozen eval): the KONIQ-trained MobileCLIP2-S0 adapter
provides a real continuous score, while the deployable defect head is the
zero-ROM calibrated measurement rule. It proves the frozen protocol reproduces
the reference numbers inside algo_agent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

import numpy as np

from . import clip_backbone, common, measure_lib


def run(ctx, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    import torch

    cfg = dict(config or {})
    C = common.plugin_config()
    inputs = common.load_eval_inputs(ctx.data_dir)
    device = common.resolve_device() or torch.device("cpu")
    t0 = time.time()

    pretrained = C.pretrained_ckpt()
    ckpt = Path(cfg.get("score_ckpt") or C.adapter_ckpt())
    if not Path(pretrained).exists() or not ckpt.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing backbone ({pretrained}) or adapter ({ckpt})")

    adapter, info = clip_backbone.load_trained_adapter(ckpt, pretrained, device)
    encoder = adapter.model

    cache = Path(common.cache_dir(ctx))
    paths = [r["path"] for r in inputs]
    feats = clip_backbone.extract_features(encoder, adapter.preprocess_val, paths, device,
                                           cache_dir=cache, tag="mobileclip2s0_lora_256",
                                           batch_size=int(cfg.get("feature_batch", 32)))
    with torch.no_grad():
        scores = adapter.head(torch.tensor(feats, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)).cpu().numpy()
    scores = np.clip(scores * 100.0, 0.0, 100.0)

    thr = C.measure_thresholds()
    defect_map = measure_lib.measure_defects_cached(paths, thr, C.DEFECTS, cache_dir=cache)

    rows = [common.make_pred(r["path"], float(scores[i]), defect_map[r["path"]])
            for i, r in enumerate(inputs)]
    common.write_preds(ctx, rows)

    visual_params = sum(p.numel() for p in adapter.model.visual.parameters())
    head_params = sum(p.numel() for p in adapter.head.parameters())
    rom = C.rom_estimate((visual_params + head_params) / 1e6)
    return {
        "method": "mobileclip2_v7_score", "split": getattr(ctx, "split", "test"),
        "seed": int(getattr(ctx, "seed", 0) or 0), "n_eval": len(rows), "synthetic": False,
        "device": str(device), "rom_params_millions": round((visual_params + head_params) / 1e6, 3),
        "rom": rom, "ckpt": str(ckpt), "ckpt_info": info,
        "wall_clock_s": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
        "metrics": {"n_eval": len(rows)},
        "note": "trained MobileCLIP2-S0 adapter score + measurement defect head (reproduction baseline)",
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit("run through algo_agent.execution.method_worker")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""IQA domain configuration for the algo_agent business plugin.

Single source of truth for the light dual-output IQA task: the defect taxonomy,
the acceptance floors, the ROM budget and the resolution of the real local
assets (frozen benchmark, pretrained MobileCLIP2-S0 / trained adapter).

The parent workspace (``.../QAA``) holds the real IQA material produced by the
``iqa_agent`` research engine.  Everything resolves local-first with an env
override (``QAA_ROOT``) so the plugin also runs when the workspace is moved.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

# ---- defect taxonomy (from the IQA requirement report) --------------------
DEFECTS: List[str] = ["blur", "over_exp", "under_exp", "flare", "white_balance"]
DEFECT_ZH: Dict[str, str] = {
    "blur": "模糊", "over_exp": "过曝", "under_exp": "欠曝",
    "flare": "炫光", "white_balance": "白平衡",
}
SEVERITY: Dict[int, str] = {0: "none", 1: "light", 2: "medium", 3: "heavy"}
WB_DIRECTIONS: List[str] = ["cool", "warm", "green", "magenta"]

# ---- acceptance floors (report ch.4 / ch.10) ------------------------------
ROM_BUDGET_MB: float = float(os.environ.get("ROM_BUDGET_MB", 60.0))
SCORE_PLCC_FLOOR: float = 0.90
SCORE_SRCC_FLOOR: float = 0.90
DEFECT_MACROF1_FLOOR: float = 0.85
HARDCASE_F1_FLOOR: float = 0.85
GRADE_AGREEMENT_FLOOR: float = 0.90
DEPLOY_PARAMS_MILLIONS: float = float(os.environ.get("DEPLOY_PARAMS_MILLIONS", 11.46))

# ---- real-MOS (KonIQ-10k) track floors ------------------------------------
# The requirement report's PLCC/SRCC target is defined against *real* human MOS
# (the trained adapter reproduced KonIQ val PLCC 0.909 / test 0.818 there).  On
# that quality-only track the defect F1 / hardcase / grade gates do not apply
# (KonIQ ships no defect annotations), so the acceptance floors are the two
# rank-correlation metrics the user asked for.
QUALITY_PLCC_FLOOR: float = float(os.environ.get("IQA_QUALITY_PLCC_FLOOR", 0.85))
QUALITY_SRCC_FLOOR: float = float(os.environ.get("IQA_QUALITY_SRCC_FLOOR", 0.85))

# A defect class needs at least this many ground-truth positives on the frozen
# eval split to be *measurable*; below it the class F1 is undefined (the
# convention below scores 0) and the all-class macro is structurally capped.
MIN_CLASS_SUPPORT: int = 5

# score -> grade bucket for the 分档一致率 (grade agreement) metric
GRADE_BINS = [(85.0, "excellent"), (70.0, "good"), (50.0, "fair"), (0.0, "poor")]

# ---- workspace / asset resolution -----------------------------------------
PLUGIN_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = PLUGIN_DIR.parent.parent            # .../algo_agent
_WORKSPACE_DEFAULT = REPO_ROOT.parent           # .../QAA


def qaa_root() -> Path:
    """Parent workspace that holds the real IQA assets (env-overridable)."""
    return Path(os.environ.get("QAA_ROOT", str(_WORKSPACE_DEFAULT)))


def iqa_agent_dir() -> Path:
    return qaa_root() / "iqa_agent"


def benchmark_dir() -> Path:
    return iqa_agent_dir() / "_work" / "benchmark"


def registry_dir() -> Path:
    return iqa_agent_dir() / "_work" / "registry"


def dev_jsonl() -> Path:
    return benchmark_dir() / "dev.jsonl"


def eval_jsonl() -> Path:
    return benchmark_dir() / "eval.jsonl"


def measure_thresholds_path() -> Path:
    return registry_dir() / "measure_thresholds.json"


def baseline_report_path() -> Path:
    return registry_dir() / "baseline.json"


def _first_existing(*candidates: Path) -> Path:
    for c in candidates:
        if Path(c).exists():
            return Path(c)
    return Path(candidates[0])

score ground truth is severity-quantised pseudo-MOS, not a real MOS panel: PLCC/SRCC read low and any PLCC discrepancy across runs must be re-checked before it is believed.

primary metric is PLCC; the score targets are a severity-quantised pseudo-MOS (good images get a filename-hash score in 88.0-95.9 that is not derivable from pixels), so a high PLCC requires near-perfect 4-level severity classification and has a structural ceiling below the defect-oriented framing suggests.

optimization_plan.change: Train the score head with a pairwise ranking term on top of MSE (loss = MSE(score, mos) + lambda * margin-rank loss over (i, j) pairs with |mos_i - mos_j| > delta), because PLCC/SRCC are rank statistics while MSE only optimises calibration.
optimization_plan.why_now: plcc/srcc are the gates with the largest gap.
optimization_plan.expected_effect: rank correlation up without retraining the encoder; calibration reported separately
optimization_plan.risk: pairwise loss can collapse the score scale -> watch MAE/grade agreement

optimization_plan.change: Replace the plain BCE with class-balanced asymmetric focal BCE: pos_weight_d = clip(N_neg / N_pos, 1.0, max_pos_weight) computed per class on the train split, focal gamma 1.5, and a per-class decision threshold tuned on the subject-disjoint val split by F1 maximisation.

concrete_params.threshold_tuning: val-split F1 max, one threshold per class

optimization_plan.why_now: generalises the class-balance fix for any class the loop flags next.
optimization_plan.expected_effect: rare-class recall up; guard precision with the per-class threshold
optimization_plan.risk: over-predicting rare classes inflates FP on the frequent classes

optimization_plan.target: stability + generalisation on the 410-row dev split
optimization_plan.change: Longer, better-regularised head training: warmup 5% + cosine decay, EMA of head weights, early stop on val macro-F1 with patience 20, gradient accumulation to an effective batch >= 64, fp16 autocast, and encoder unfreezing scheduled so the last N transformer blocks train only after the head has stabilised.
optimization_plan.why_now: the current 40-120 epoch heads are the only trainable part, so schedule quality is cheap to improve
optimization_plan.expected_effect: lower variance across iterations; PLCC/F1 less seed-sensitive
optimization_plan.risk: longer training overfits a 410-row dev split -> keep the subject-disjoint val gate

optimization_plan.change: Keep the trained 5-way defect head as the primary head but distil the calibrated rule/measure features into it (feature-level distillation on flare), so the single deployed head does not regress to the rule head's 0 FLARE F1.
optimization_plan.why_now: the rule head cannot separate flare at all while the adapter head can
optimization_plan.expected_effect: flare F1 kept while ROM stays inside the budget
optimization_plan.risk: feature concatenation adds parameters -> re-check the 60 MB fp16 ROM gate

annotation.goal: Turn the local VLM from an unvalidated helper into a review-assisted labeller that raises the positive count for the classes the frozen eval cannot measure (white_balance 0, flare 9), without ever treating a model output as ground truth.

client.output_schema: {path, ok, defects{d:{present,severity[,direction]}}, quality_score_0_100, confidence_0_1, model_id, prompt_version, elapsed_s, usage, review_required: true, provenance}
client.invariant: review_required is always true - pre-labels never enter a dataset version unreviewed

tuning_steps: prompt v2 for blur: ask the model for an edge-energy / high-frequency check and a centre-vs-corner crop comparison before deciding blur; v1 blur P/R was 0.25/0.20 on the 20-image pilot.

add an explicit negative guard for flare and white_balance: require a described light source / cast direction; v1 flagged 4 flare FP and 6 white_balance FP on the same 20 images, so its positive rate is unusable without the guard.
require the wb direction (cool/warm/green/magenta) and reject any white_balance=present without a direction; wb_direction_acc was not measurable in v1 (0 GT positives).
run the pilot per class in batches of 20-30, keep the prompt_version in provenance, and only promote a prompt version when its agreement on a 30-image human-reviewed set beats the previous one.

review_protocol.rare_classes: flare, white_balance -> 100% human review of every pre-label
review_protocol.other_classes: >= 30% stratified human review (stratified by model confidence)
review_protocol.accept_rule: a pre-label is accepted only after a human accept/edit; disagreement is logged and drives the next prompt version
review_protocol.audit: store model_id + prompt_version + reviewer + accept/edit/reject in the row provenance
review_protocol.kpi: human review time per accepted label, and the pre-label accept rate per class

augmentation.goal: Fill the measurable-support gaps for the classes the frozen eval cannot score, then re-freeze.
rules: augment only the train split; the frozen eval is never augmented in the same protocol version
every augmented sample keeps provenance (source image id + transform + parameters)
bump dataset_version and re-run the reference baseline after any augmentation release

methods: channel-gain (von Kries-style) transforms of clean images at measured colour temperatures, verified by estimating the cast direction back
real captures collected with grey-card reference for ground-truth direction
white_balance.note: cover cool/warm/green/magenta roughly balanced; a class with 0 positives today is the single biggest structural cap on the macro-F1 gate.

methods: physically-plausible veiling-glare / ghost overlays whose PSF is estimated from the real flare positives
vary intensity in the same 0/1/2/3 severity scale as the taxonomy
flare.note: mix synthetic with real captures; keep a small human-reviewed synthetic holdout to catch an overlay artifact the metric would otherwise reward.

methods: gamma/curve-based darkening with highlight preservation, severity-matched to the existing labels
motion-blur kernels (direction + length) and defocus disks, severity-matched

acceptance: after augmentation, re-run measure_threshold + the best adapter on the re-frozen eval
only promote the new dataset version if the reference baseline improves or holds on every class that was already measurable
